title: mascot 0.1.0
text: 72 × 105 = 7,560 per-subject bundle files present different constraints HCP1065 atlas. Key design choices trade-offs: One release per bundle (72 releases, tractseg-<bundle_name>). Putting 7,560 files single release unwieldy (GitHub UI, API pagination, accidental full-release downloads). One release per bundle gives users clean, addressable unit enables partial re-runs specific bundles need updated. GitHub Actions matrix parallelism (72 concurrent jobs). runner processes exactly one bundle end--end (fetch → convert → upload), full 72-bundle conversion completes roughly time slowest single bundle rather 72 × time. HTTP range requests instead full archive download. Zenodo archive large ZIP file. data-raw/zip_index.py reads ZIP central directory (two small HTTP range requests), data-raw/fetch_bundle.py fetches .trk entry individually via range request. avoids downloading gigabytes data per runner keeps per-job bandwidth proportional bundle size. compress = "gzip" instead "xz". 105 files serialise per job (72 jobs running parallel CI), gzip’s faster compression better trade-: wall-clock time CI reduced size penalty relative XZ modest (typically 10–20 %). End-user download sizes remain acceptable release fetched bundle--bundle import_bundle(). Parallel mclapply within runner. Subject-level TRK → RDS conversion embarrassingly parallel; parallel::mclapply exploits cores available GitHub-hosted runner (typically 2) halve per-bundle conversion time. Empty-TRK guard. TRK file whose size ≤ 1,000 bytes contains header streamlines. files silently skipped rather producing corrupt .rds, keeping subject count accurate.
